newsitem.title: USA: Man gets 60 years for attack on pregnant student.
newsitem.headline: Man gets 60 years for attack on pregnant student.

text.p: A former New Mexico university instructor who kidnapped and sexually assaulted an eight-months-pregnant student was sentenced Friday to almost 60 years in prison.
State District Judge Thomas Cornish sent Eduardo Araiza, 27, to 59-1/2 years in jail for the 1995 attack against Jennifer McBrayer, one of his students at New Mexico State University.
Then aged 22, McBrayer went to Araiza's home to pick up an assignment but was shocked in the neck with a stun gun as she stood at the front door.

Araiza then handcuffed and gagged her before dragging her into a bathtub and sexually assaulting her for two hours. Araiza stuck a knife into her throat and held it there for several minutes but then suddenly dropped the knife, uncuffed her and let her go, prosecutors said.
Araiza, a struggling poet who portrayed himself as a bohemian, pleaded temporary insanity but a jury convicted him on seven counts last September.
McBrayer survived the attack and one month later gave birth to a healthy baby girl. In a letter to the Las Cruces court, she asked that Araiza be given the maximum sentence.
"I only survived because of luck, the grace of God and stubborn determination," she said.
With good behaviour in prison, Araiza could be released after 30 years.
